tool_analysis:
Step Analysis: Recorded browser session navigated the Magento Admin Shipments grid, applied column filters (Shipment #, Order #, Ship to Name, Total Qty from/to), clicked Search, exported the grid (CSV/Excel/XML), used the mass-action dropdown to select 'PDF Packingslips' and submitted it, and opened a shipment 'View' page. The run captured stable element hashes for the most important controls and produced robust header-based XPath fallbacks.

Task Definition: Implement a deterministic, re-usable tool that: 1) opens the admin shipments grid, 2) applies the specified filters, 3) triggers an export in the chosen format, 4) selects visible rows and applies a specified mass action, and 5) opens the specified shipment's View page and returns identifying info.

Action Plan:
- Navigate to the shipments grid URL.
- Fill the filter inputs (Shipment #, Order #, Ship to Name, Total Qty from/to) using recorded element hashes for determinism.
- Click Search and wait for the grid to refresh.
- Set Export format (select) and click the Export button (using recorded element hashes).
- Click 'Select Visible' to mark the visible rows, choose the requested mass-action option from the mass-action select (recorded element hash), and click Submit to apply it.
- Wait for processing and then open the row-scoped 'View' link for the requested visible shipment number using a robust XPath based on the shipment's visible number and the href pattern.
- Extract the shipment view page title and internal shipment id from the URL to confirm success.

Variable Identification (tool inputs):
- base_url: base admin URL (required). Used to build the initial navigation.
- shipment_increment_id: visible Shipment # filter.
- order_increment_id: visible Order # filter.
- ship_to_name: Ship to Name filter.
- total_qty_from / total_qty_to: numeric range for Total Qty filter.
- export_format: CSV, Excel or XML - the export format to use.
- mass_action_option: visible mass action text to select (PDF Packingslips or Print Shipping Labels).
- view_shipment_number: visible Shipment # to open the View link for verification.

Step Optimization: 
- Prefer deterministic element hashes captured from a successful session where available for inputs/selects/buttons (these are included for the key fields: filter inputs, Search, Export select/button, massaction select/submit). These reduce fragile text-only matching errors.
- Use XPath row-scoped selector for the View link (by displayed shipment number + '/sales_shipment/view/shipment_id/' href contains) because the View link's href pattern is stable across Magento installs and avoids depending on per-row element hashes (which vary by row).
- Re-query the DOM after navigations (explicit wait steps included) to handle DOM refreshes after Search/Export/Mass-action.
- Avoid fragile CSS pseudo-selectors (:contains/:has) that some frameworks don't support; when we must match by visible text we use XPath normalize-space() matches.

Notes and Limitations:
- The tool assumes the automation context is already authenticated as Magento admin (recorded session was logged in). No login steps are included.
- Element hashes recorded in the session (elementHash values) are used for determinism; if the target instance has different DOM than the recorded session you should re-run a small verification step that these selectors resolve to exactly one element before using the tool in production.
- The tool performs the full demo sequence (filters → Search → Export → Mass-action → View). All input parameters listed are expected to be supplied; they control the executed values. For environments with localized labels or customized admin themes, prefer verifying id/name attributes and adapt the elementHash or XPath values accordingly.

Selector robustness guidance: always verify each XPath/elementHash resolves to exactly one element in your automation environment; prefer attribute-based selectors (id/name) if they exist and are stable. This tool uses recorded high-confidence element hashes and row-scoped XPath for the variable View link to maximize reliability.
name: magento_admin_shipments_tool
description: Automates locating shipments in Magento 1.x admin shipments grid using header-anchored selectors; applies filters, performs CSV/Excel/XML export, runs a mass-action (e.g. PDF Packingslips), and opens a shipment 'View' page. Uses deterministic element hashes recorded during a successful session where available, and robust XPath fallbacks anchored on visible column headers / href patterns.

steps.description: Open the Magento Admin Shipments grid page (starting point for all actions).
Enter the Shipment # filter value into the Shipment filter input (element captured as a16414da11).
Enter the Order # filter value into the Order filter input (element captured as 28b46dc009).
Enter the Ship to Name filter value into the Ship to Name filter input (element captured as 6ae9a2d6cc).
Enter Total Qty 'From' filter value into the corresponding input (element captured as 0bab1b22e0).
Enter Total Qty 'To' filter value into the corresponding input (element captured as c1e188c737).
Click the Search button to apply filters and refresh the grid (Search button captured as f7e7049ec).
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
Choose the export format in the Export select (export select captured as b9908203f9).
Click the Export action/button to trigger the grid export (export button captured as 2707c7ca5b).
Wait briefly for export handling to complete and for the page/DOM to settle (re-query DOM after this step in subsequent steps).
Click the 'Select Visible' link to check all visible row checkboxes. Uses visible-text XPath (fallback when a deterministic elementHash for this link wasn't recorded).
Select the mass-action option (e.g. 'PDF Packingslips') in the Actions dropdown (mass-action select captured as f61b130718).
Click the mass-action Submit button to apply the selected action to the selected rows (submit button captured as 943f4566ab).
Wait for mass-action processing to complete and the grid to refresh.
Open the shipment detail by clicking the 'View' link in the row whose visible Shipment # equals {view_shipment_number}. Uses a row-scoped XPath (href contains '/sales_shipment/view/shipment_id/').
Wait for the shipment View page to load.
Extract essential information from the opened Shipment View page (title and internal shipment id from URL).
steps.goal: Return the shipment View page title and the shipment internal id (extracted from the View URL) so the caller can verify navigation succeeded.

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL (protocol+host) for the Magento instance, for example: "http://dockerized-magento.local". The tool will navigate to {base_url}/index.php/admin/sales_shipment/.

input_schema.name: shipment_increment_id
input_schema.description: Shipment increment id to filter by (visible 'Shipment #' column), e.g. "100000003". If not needed use an empty string "" but the demo run expects a value.

input_schema.name: order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Order increment id to filter by (visible 'Order #' column), e.g. "100000206". Provide an empty string "" if not used.

input_schema.name: ship_to_name
input_schema.description: Ship-to name filter (visible 'Ship to Name' column), e.g. "John Doe". Provide empty string "" if not used.

input_schema.name: total_qty_from
input_schema.description: Total Qty 'From' filter value (integer as string), e.g. "2". Provide empty string "" if not used.

input_schema.name: total_qty_to
input_schema.description: Total Qty 'To' filter value (integer as string), e.g. "5". Provide empty string "" if not used.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Export format to use for the grid export. Must be one of: 'CSV', 'Excel', 'XML'.

input_schema.name: mass_action_option
input_schema.description: Visible text of the mass-action option to apply (choose the exact option text from the Actions dropdown).

input_schema.name: view_shipment_number
input_schema.description: Displayed Shipment # (visible in the grid) for the row whose 'View' link should be opened after mass-action, e.g. "100000003".
